title: MemSeer: Leverage Memory Failure Distinctions and Multi-Grained Prediction in Ultra-Scale Heterogeneous X86/ARM Clusters
problem: In ultra-scale heterogeneous cloud clusters mixing x86 and ARM platforms, DRAM failures are a primary cause of server downtime; existing prediction methods fail to account for architecture-specific failure patterns and require single-scale predictions.
motivation: DRAM reliability is critical for service-level agreements in large-scale data centers, but heterogeneous architectures exhibit distinct failure modes requiring architecture-aware, multi-grained prediction approaches.
method: MemSeer predicts memory chip failures in data-center clusters using both x86 and ARM processors (two different chip architectures), by recognizing that each fails in different ways. It monitors warning signs at multiple time scales (from hours to weeks ahead) and feeds predictions to automated systems that can replace failing chips before outages occur. This improves prediction accuracy by 17.3% and catches 27% more failures.
key_novelty: Predicting memory failures works better by recognizing that different processor types like x86 and ARM fail in distinct ways and monitoring multiple time scales.
contributions: In-depth analysis of memory failure characteristics across x86/ARM architectures
Multi-grained prediction approach capturing failure patterns at multiple timescales
17.3% F1-score improvement, 27% average recall gain, 42.7% VM interruption reduction in real-world deployment
